name: Rising Evil
caption: A kendo-cane-wielding tag team locked in a running feud with The Creeps all summer.

name: The Creeps
caption: A tag team locked in a running feud with the kendo-cane-wielding Rising Evil all summer.

name: The Vegas Badasses

tenures.note: Formed at Vegas Violence (7 September 2001), when Paddy O'Shea knocked down his own manager and took a beer from Dirk Western mid-match. Lost to Demonic G-Gangsta on 10 January the debuting 28th Street 24 January. drifted apart in 2002; paired with brother Father Frank as Fighting O'Sheas 16 May, same card which lost singles grudge match.

caption: Dirk Western and Paddy O'Shea, who formed the team mid-match at Vegas Violence in September 2001 and reunited in 2003 against The Rodeo Boys, with Western by then a ringside commentator.

name: The Rhombus

tenures.note: Loses a six-man tag, all three men billed together as The Rhombus, to The Mighty Men and a returning Paddy O'Shea at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), Evil Capsman submitting to O'Shea's own Chicken Wing. Capsman and Evil Capsman fight G-Gangsta and Sebastian to a no contest on March To Hell (21 October 2004), broken up by Sonicman and The Maquilladora. Wins over The Mighty Men and a returning Paddy O'Shea on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), Capsman pinning O'Shea with the Capitol Punishment. Billed The Rhombus with a fourth man, The Maquilladora, in an eight-man elimination loss to the Riders of the Apocalypse on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004), Sebastian pinning The Maquilladora after Robbie Caldwell's own outside tazer shot.

caption: A veteran Las Vegas tag team, VWF Tag Team Champions as far back as 2003 across a title lineage that also passed briefly through Randall Crane and Classy Joey Boy before ending for good at Vegas Violence III, when the returning stable The Circle cost them the belts against the Rodeo Boys; disqualified against the newly formed Dudes of Destruction on Xtreme Prejudice VI after a broken surfboard drew a referee's ire.

name: The Rodeo Boys

tenures.note: Loses the VWF Tag Team Championship to Hot Property in a Flashback ambush on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then wins the Dog Day One tag team battle royal. Loses the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round to Marcus O'Malley wrestling alone, then is beaten down by Hot Property and Flash in a special Flashback before competing in the sixteen-man tag scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), Kenny Kidd falling from the ladder alongside Stevie Knight. Reported gone for good after Billy Bones's own contract release on Wrestle Style V.3, the pair are reinstated to the VWF on the spot at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004) after lawyer RAR intervenes with majority owner Kingston Cash, then immediately beat down new VWF Tag Team Champions Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen with cowbells. Loses a VWF Tag Team Championship match by disqualification after Kenny Kidd brands Marcus O'Malley on March To Hell (21 October 2004). Loses the title rematch to a substitute Outlaw Morris Bass and Mark McQueen on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), Billy Bones submitting to the Devils Snare. Wins a weapons-advantage Number One Contenders match over The Mighty Men at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), Bones branding The Reckoning's face and pinning The Salvation. Interferes to help the Riders of the Apocalypse beat down Iyasu Saku and jump Paddy O'Shea on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004), read by the broadcast's own commentary as the pair joining the group; helps eliminate Capsman first in the eight-man Rhombus/Riders of the Apocalypse match before both members are eliminated themselves. Both eliminated separately from the tag team title battle royal on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), Kenny Kidd by mystery entrant Thunder Valenkov and Billy Bones by a returning Sonicman. Billy Bones loses to Sonicman on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005); the pair works over The Reckoning's ankle together during Kenny Kidd's own title-feud win the same night.

Announced their own retirement at Xtreme Machine I (8 March 2006, an earlier pass). Returned to make the save for a beaten Joey Young and Tom Rogers against POT on New Year's Eve of Destruction 2006, then beat POT (Lark Fenriz and Foodstamp) by pinfall on Sin City Fights February 7, billing it their own 'last ride' and challenging the O'Malleys, Team Brittania and Hot Property to a one-night tag team tournament.

caption: Kenny Kidd and Billy Bones' own tag team, first teaming in vwf-vegas-2003, then reuniting in VXW as previously three-time VXW tag champions, losing their first match back together to Team Essington, then losing a four-way tornado tag to Purgatory at Fear Is Coming II.

name: The Circle
notes: A heel stable led by the returning "Dark Monster" Tai Angela and his manager Blackbird, first appearing unnamed (breaking up a six-man tag match and declaring a "New Age of Darkness") at Vegas Violence III and taking the name The Circle on Firestorm 10-21-03; Iyasu Saku and Man Mountain Samuri (repackaged as "Colossus") joined from the disbanded tag team Rising Evil.
caption: A team on Vegas Wrestling Federation's own cards from 2003-10.

name: The Legends of the VWF
notes: Sebastian and G-Gangsta's own team, formed when Gangsta interrupted Sebastian's handicap match against Rob Beauty and Kevin Blair the week before Vegas Violence III; won that debut match by pinfall, challenged for the VWF Tag Team Championship by disqualification on Firestorm 10-21-03, and were signed for a handicap match against Ric Beauty for a future special with a further tag title shot at stake.
caption: A team on Vegas Wrestling Federation's own cards from 2003-10.

name: Desolation Row
notes: Entered the 12 Days Tournament's own debut tag bracket, beating the Rodeo Boys by disqualification after Billy Bones went to a ringside cowbell.
caption: Entered the 12 Days Tournament's own debut tag bracket, beating the Rodeo Boys by disqualification after Billy Bones went to a ringside cowbell.

name: The Fallen Angels
notes: Entered the 12 Days Tournament's own debut tag bracket, beating the New Age Army (Iyasu Saku and Colossus) when Insomniac reversed the Good and Evil Crossface into the Insomnia Cure on Saku.
caption: Entered the 12 Days Tournament's own debut tag bracket, beating the New Age Army (Iyasu Saku and Colossus) when Insomniac reversed the Good and Evil Crossface into the Insomnia Cure on Saku.

name: 28th Street
notes: Entered the 12 Days Tournament's own debut tag bracket, losing to the ad hoc pairing of Jushin Liger GOLD and El Gringo Loco.
caption: Entered the 12 Days Tournament's own debut tag bracket, losing to the ad hoc pairing of Jushin Liger GOLD and El Gringo Loco.

name: The Lynch Mob
caption: A returning heel duo, billed as feared veterans of the sport, who debuted on the Kickoff Card by attacking the Legends of the VWF and demanding a Tag Team Championship shot.
notes: In-fiction billed as returning after a long absence, with a self-described history of ending careers and "shutting down promotions"; no document read by this lane, or noted in any prior wave's own findings.md, corroborates that history against any other held wing, including an unrelated, unstructured faction of the same name in the 1998 wing EWWF East.

name: The Enforcers
caption: An enhancement team squashed by the debuting Lynch Mob in twelve seconds on Firestorm, January 19, 2004, with no individual member named in that broadcast; Dane Klingel and Rob Kidane wrestled under the same banner and lost to the Society of Doom on Firestorm, February 26, 2004.

identity.note: Name collision only with a differently themed stable of the same name in another held wing, formed later the same year around real-world political figures; no member name or date ties the two.

name: Jumping Jacks Flash
caption: An enhancement pairing of two similarly-named jobbers, pinned by The Unholy Alliance in the team's own lone attested appearance.

tenures.note: Runs in on Evil Capsman on Firestorm (27 May 2004), announcing new individual ring names, Jack Smash and Jack Blast, then competes in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal and the Dog Days Tag Team Elimination match, losing both.

name: The Unholy Alliance
caption: A tag pairing of the large, silent Dementia and the outspoken Mistress, whose win over Jumping Jacks Flash led into video evidence of a Lynch Mob bribery scheme and a Gauntlet four-way Tag Team Championship match.

tenures.note: Dementia and The Mistress compete in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal, eliminated after Dementia saves his partner. Eliminated from the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round by The Mighty Men, then eliminated from the Dog Days tournament in the Tag Team Elimination Ladder Match on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004).

notes: Previously named only in rumor at Ghost Town Blues, without a confirmed appearance or id; this broadcast is the pairing's first confirmed physical appearance.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (the-unholy-alliance-gxw-2001); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Society of Doom
caption: Kevin Simmons's own stable, billed together on the Gauntlet as McQueen and O'Malley beat Sonicman and the Original Masked Man in the group's first on-screen billing as a unit.

tenures.note: Mark McQueen and Marcus O'Malley beat Blaze and The Real Deal on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then compete in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal, eliminated in a mutual elimination with Orion; leader Kevin Simmons announces his own in-character retirement the same Firestorm broadcast. Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen win the sixteen-man Dog Days 3 tag scramble together on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), O'Malley unhooking the suspended ring; O'Malley alone had wrestled the Dog Day Two tag bracket for the team the week before, McQueen barred from competing. Billed a Society of Doom member in his own Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004) ring introduction, Adam Jennings wins the VWF 24 Hour Championship from Kevin Blair; The Outlaw Morris Bass runs in alongside Jennings, O'Malley and McQueen, all named on commentary as the Society of Doom, to save Kevin Simmons from a Kingston Cash chair attack during the night's own ladder match. Kevin Simmons and Outlaw Morris Bass win by disqualification over The Mighty Men on March To Hell (21 October 2004). Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen chase off a backstage beatdown of Simmons on March To Hell II (28 October 2004). All four -- Simmons, O'Malley, McQueen and Adam Jennings -- enter the Rage in the Cage together as the Society of Doom at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), Simmons pinning O'Malley to become the new co-holder of the VWF Tag Team Championship. Adam Jennings and Mark McQueen, both billed members, help fight off the Riders of the Apocalypse in a post-match brawl after Jennings retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004). Kevin Simmons and Marcus O'Malley are confirmed suspended from the VWF by New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), leaving only Jennings and McQueen active.

identity.note: Shares a name exactly with a differently-rostered VXW stable formed nearly two years later around a different leader; no document connects them.

notes: Kevin Simmons and Kagedo were already established as fellow Society of Doom members as far back as Firestorm (26 Feb 2004), per that broadcast's own text; this pass mints the unit at its first on-screen billing by name, with Simmons introduced as its leader.

name: The Mighty Men
caption: A debuting big-man tag team, eliminated from the Dog Day One tag team battle royal after The Salvation was big-booted out by The Real Deal.

tenures.note: Wins the Dog Day Two tag team tournament, beating the Unholy Alliance and CAPSMEN! in the first round and Marcus O'Malley wrestling alone in the final, then competes in the sixteen-man tag scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004). Part of a six-man brawl with Capsmen, Iyasu Saku and Sonicman ruled a no contest on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004). Loses to Alcoholics Anonymous (Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen) by disqualification on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) after isolating an injured McQueen, then runs in to break up a Capsman near-fall on Real Deal during the VWF Tag Team Championship match, handing Blaze and Real Deal the disqualification win. The Salvation publicly refuses Kingston Cash's own proposed tag-title handicap-match stipulation on the team's behalf on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004), then helps clear the ring after Adam Jennings retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship; The Reckoning loses a straight singles match to Mark McQueen the same night. Both men enter the tag team title battle royal on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), The Salvation triple-teamed out by the Riders of the Apocalypse after The Reckoning leaves him to challenge mystery entrant Thunder Valenkov, who eliminates The Reckoning moments later. The Reckoning taps out to Kenny Kidd's own Ankle Lock on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), suffering ligament damage.

name: CAPSMEN!
caption: A superhero-costumed tag pairing of Capsman and Evil Capsman, attested teaming together in a 24 Hour Championship battle royal and a losing VWF Tag Team Championship challenge.

tenures.note: Help eliminate champion Kevin Blair early from the VWF 24 Hour Championship battle royal on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004). Lose a VWF Tag Team Championship match to Blaze and Real Deal by disqualification on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) after The Mighty Men run in, then are beaten down by The Mighty Men regardless. Fight G-Gangsta and Sebastian to a no contest on March To Hell (21 October 2004), the match voided after Robbie Caldwell and Iyasu Saku run in for a four-on-two beatdown. Loses to Sebastian and Robbie Caldwell on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), the winners earning the right to book their own matches at Ghost Town Blues.

name: Alcoholics Anonymous
caption: A joke tag name for Society of Doom members Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen, billed once on Wrestle Style V.6 before the pairing won the VWF Tag Team Championship from Blaze and Real Deal at Vegas Violence IV.

tenures.note: Billed once by this name on Wrestle Style V.6. Wins the VWF Tag Team Championship from Blaze and Real Deal at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), Mark McQueen submitting Real Deal with the Devils Snare; the Rodeo Boys, reinstated on the spot by majority owner Kingston Cash at lawyer RAR's own urging, beat down both new champions immediately after. Retains the VWF Tag Team Championship on March To Hell (21 October 2004) when Kenny Kidd is disqualified for branding Marcus O'Malley with an iron.

name: Riders of the Apocalypse
caption: A four-man stable of Sebastian, G-Gangsta, Robbie Caldwell and Iyasu Saku, feuding with the Society of Doom over the VWF 24 Hour Championship.

tenures.note: Named as a four-man group on March To Hell (21 October 2004), interfering to help Sebastian and G-Gangsta against Capsman and Evil Capsman, then unable to save Iyasu Saku from Adam Jennings's own VWF 24 Hour Championship defense. Loses members to individual matches on March To Hell II (28 October 2004) -- G-Gangsta to Fast Eddie Cutlass, Robbie Caldwell to Randall Crane, Iyasu Saku to Classy Joey Boy -- and offers a fourth membership slot to Classy Joey Boy, who turns on Sebastian, G-Gangsta and Caldwell instead. Beats down stablemate Iyasu Saku in an apparent staged play on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004), the returning Rodeo Boys jumping Paddy O'Shea afterward and, by the broadcast's own account, joining the group; loses the eight-man Rhombus/Riders of the Apocalypse elimination match's own final fall to Sebastian, the last man standing, and Robbie Caldwell loses the VWF 24 Hour Championship match to Adam Jennings the same night. Enters the tag team title battle royal five men strong on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), eliminated one by one until only Sebastian remains, beaten by mystery entrant Thunder Valenkov. G-Gangsta fails to appear for a six-man tag on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), instead returning after the bell to beat down Sebastian and publicly resign from the group. Runs in on former member G-Gangsta -- teamed with Fast Eddie Cutlass against Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov -- on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), Sebastian, Robbie Caldwell and the Rodeo Boys stretchering him out of the building. Now four strong with Robbie Caldwell, Kenny Kidd, Billy Bones and the debuting Mad Bomber, sweeping March To Madness (2 March 2005): Caldwell beats Thunder Valenkov after Kidd distracts the referee and the Mad Bomber blinds Valenkov with a smoke bomb and chairs him, Kidd beats Fast Eddie Cutlass, and the debuting Mad Bomber beats Lark Fenriz. Demands matches for Billy Bones and The Mad Bomber from John Tyler backstage at The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005); enters the wing's own closing Gauntlet battle royal with only Robbie Caldwell representing the group, Kenny Kidd having already been eliminated from the eight-man elimination match earlier on the same card and Billy Bones and The Mad Bomber never entering the battle royal at all.

name: Trinity
caption: A heel stable led by Gods Tears, formerly billed Orion The Hunter, uniting The Equalizer and the unmasked Pagan around the VWF Heavyweight and Submission Championships and Melanie Kilpatrick's own kidnapping.

tenures.note: Named on commentary through Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), closing that broadcast standing together over a bloodied Lark Fenriz, Jason Storm and Classy Joey Boy after The Equalizer's own VWF Heavyweight Championship win. Wins a six-man tag over Jason Storm, Fast Eddie Cutlass and Flash on March To Hell (21 October 2004), the group's own Pagan unmasked on air for the first time. Briefly inducts Flash as a fourth member on March To Hell II (28 October 2004) before turning on him mid-promo and beating him unconscious; the same night Gods Tears wins a non-title count-out over The Maquilladora, boasting on air about the group's own formation, and Pagan is revealed as Melanie Kilpatrick's own kidnapper during the post-show chaos that follows Jason Storm's ambush of The Equalizer. Gods Tears wins the VWF Submission Championship and The Equalizer retains the VWF Heavyweight Championship in the Rage in the Cage at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), Pagan interfering in the final fall after separately crippling Jason Storm in an unsanctioned cage trap.

name: Triple X

tenures.note: Lost the Tag Team Championship to Blaze and Real Deal on 14 January and failed to regain it on 24 January and at Ghost Town Blues.

caption: Chumpy and Earthquake, two huge eaters at a combined 707 pounds, who sided with the VWF and won its Tag Team Championship in November 2001.

identity.note: Shares a common name with units and characters of other promotions; no roster, billing or chronology links them.

name: Elements of Violence

tenures.note: Jack Spade and Dage pursued the RCW through January; Dage won the 24 Hour Championship from Demonic on 24 January and lost it back at Ghost Town Blues.

caption: Jack Spade and Dage, two former RCW men who formed the Elements of Violence on the VWF's side in October 2001.

name: The Huxtables
caption: Huey Huxtable and his father Henry, who beat Tai Angela and Blackbird as a team in October 2001.

name: The Sex Icons

tenures.note: Formed when Classy Joey Boy turned on G-Gangsta and sided with Sebastian; won the vacant Tag Team Championship 20 June.

caption: Appears on RAW-Vegas's 2002 cards, from Birthday Bash (1 August) to Thunder (19 September).

name: The Sexacutioners
caption: Appears on RAW-Vegas's 2002 cards, from Thunder (24 July) to Thunder (19 September).

name: The Fighting O'Sheas

tenures.note: Formed when Paddy O'Shea's priest brother, Father Frank, returned to wrestle alongside him.

caption: Appears on RAW-Vegas's 2002 cards, on Thunder (24 July).

name: The Brute Squad
caption: Appears on RAW-Vegas's 2002 cards, from Phear Phantastic II (17 October) to Ghosts of RAW (31 October).

name: Armegeddon
caption: Appears on RAW-Vegas's 2002 cards, on Ghosts of RAW (31 October).

name: The RCW

tenures.note: An invading outside faction; ran in on the VWF Tag Team Title match on 10 January, crowned G-Gangsta its own RCW Champion on 17 January, and repeatedly interfered in title matches through Ghost Town Blues.

caption: Demonic, G-Gangsta, Blaze and the Real Deal, an invading outside faction that crowned its own RCW Championship inside the VWF in January 2002.

name: New York City Headliners

tenures.note: Managed by Barry Bronxs; feuded with 28th Street over a Tag Team Championship shot.

caption: Delicious Don Brooklynn and Terry Queenz, managed by Barry Bronxs.
